mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals an easing monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days without regime dependence.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4.0% signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE > 4.0%, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in CPIAUCSL (inflation) and decreases in FEDFUNDS (monetary easing) signal a policy response to inflation that reduces recession risk, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days through interaction effects.
failure_condition: The joint effect of CPIAUCSL rising and FEDFUNDS falling produces negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases, or the interaction term coefficient is negative and significant (p<0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During late-cycle expansions, a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 105.0 signals weakening manufacturing momentum that reduces corporate profit visibility, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In late-cycle expansions, INDPRO < 105.0 is followed by positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of cases, or Rank IC for the signal falls below 0.03 in that regime.

mechanism_narrative: A rising residential sales (RSAFS) indicates strong housing market activity that precedes broader consumer spending growth, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days without threshold conditions.
failure_condition: RSAFS growth does not correlate with positive 5-day SPX returns in more than 60% of periods, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 105.0 signals manufacturing contraction that reduces corporate earnings visibility, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO < 105.0 is followed by positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases, or Rank IC for the signal falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in employment (PAYEMS) and decreases in unemployment rate (UNRATE) signal a tight labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days through interaction effects.
failure_condition: The joint effect of PAYEMS rising and UNRATE falling produces negative 5-day returns in more than 60% of cases, or the interaction term coefficient is negative and significant (p<0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles, a federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) rise above 4.5% signals reduced liquidity and higher borrowing costs that depress equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In monetary tightening cycles, FEDFUNDS > 4.5% is followed by positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of cases, or Rank IC for the signal falls below 0.03 in that regime.
